summary:
VISUAL QA, ROUND 2: not a pass. 7 blockers, all ui. The portal signup and billing screens are now at the bar. What is left is mostly at the edges: the product apps in view only and locked states, the WMS first screen, keyboard focus on text fields, and the 404 page.

**What I did**
- Built 16 fresh accounts through the real screens with the test gateway: fresh signup, unverified trial, trial day 1, trial with 9 days left, trial ending in 2 days, trial with a card, invited member, trial ended, paid, paid with 1 seat, payment due, view only, cancel set, pause set, paused, ended.
- Took 719 screenshots in light and dark at 1440, 768 and 390, against the shared dev servers. I looked at them as contact sheets and as full size crops.
- Ran script checks on 674 of those captures for sideways scroll, small tap targets, clipped text and console errors, plus a sweep from 320 to 1280 wide.
- Measured text contrast on 20 pages in both themes, focus rings, hover and pressed states, busy states on a slow network, and reduced motion.
- Clicked the create buttons in view only and locked apps to see what opens.
- Did not restart any shared server. All six are still up. The working tree is clean.

**Round 1 blockers, rechecked**
- **Fixed, measured:**
  - No sideways scroll from 320 to 1280, with a 40 character org name.
  - One heading left edge (184 px) on every billing page.
  - Sign in screens start at one height on phones.
  - The setup guide shows 5 steps with the apps in the first screen.
  - One notice at a time, and no trial bar on day 1.
  - Invited members arrive verified with no code email.
  - No small tap targets on portal signup or billing screens.
- **Fixed, seen:** one call to action label on `/pricing`, and edge fades on the phone tab strip.
- **Partly fixed:** view only. CRM and Projects now stop you with a clear dialog before a form opens. WMS does not, and parts of Pulse do not (blocker 2).
- **Not rechecked:** the proration cent difference. I saw $23.20 in every capture this round but did not repeat the timed test.

**What is good**
- Signup, picker, verify, welcome, review, test checkout (decline and bank approval), success, billing home in every phase, plan change preview, invoices, the invoice PDF, details, team, activity, cancel and pause all look polished in both themes at all three widths.
- Banners and lock screens use the same words and button in the Portal, CRM, WMS, Projects and Pulse.
- The seat offer on the invite form works and reads well.
- Text contrast: no failure below 4.5 to 1 on any page checked.
- Busy states show within 120 ms and block a second send.
- Reduced motion stops the confetti.
- After paying, WMS and CRM dropped the red banner within 4 and 9 seconds.

**Why it fails**
1. Focus on text fields is almost invisible, and switches that are off are too faint.
2. View only WMS and parts of Pulse still open full forms.
3. A locked Projects app still opens the New task form, which dead ends.
4. The first WMS screen in a trial is a bare wall of 9 required fields.
5. Unknown portal addresses show the default 404 with no theme and no way back.
6. The Organization page truncates names and emails on phones.
7. A short list of copy and layout polish items.

**Other things seen, not blockers**
- WMS showed "Free trial. 9 days left" for at least 20 seconds after I ended the trial with the test tool. It was correct a few minutes later. The integrator disclosed a short gap here.
- The WMS dev server logs a Next.js console error (`Could not validate instant`) on `/dashboard` whenever it redirects to setup or the lock screen. It is likely dev only, which I did not confirm on a production build.
- Product app top bars (CRM, Projects, Pulse) have 32 px tap targets on phones. That is the apps' own chrome, not a billing screen.

**Not checked**
- Real Stripe pages and the Google and Microsoft buttons (no keys).
- `/signup/company`.
- The warehouse limit offer in the WMS.
- Loading skeletons.
- The "billing is off" production state, which was fine in round 1 and is covered by the integrator's e2e run.

Everything is in `/home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/visual2/` (`shots/`, `sheets/`, `audit-*.json`, `scripts/`, `notes.txt`). File names are `<screen>--<size>-<theme>.png`; the `x*` files are the interaction checks.

blockers.title: Focus on text fields is almost invisible, and off switches are too faint
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/components/ui/input.tsx (line 13, the focus-within classes); apps/portal/src/components/ui/switch.tsx; seen on /signup, /login, /billing/details, the test card form and the plan picker
blockers.detail:
Wrong: buttons, links and switches get a clear 2 px brand ring on focus, but text fields do not.
- Light: a focused field changes its border from rgb(206,199,182) to rgb(195,188,170), plus a 3 px ring of the same beige at 28%.
- Dark: the border goes from rgb(51,56,63) to rgb(58,63,70).
- That is about a 1.1 to 1 change. In dark you cannot tell which field you are in. SPEC 13 says every control has a visible focus ring.
- Switches that are off: the track against its card measures 1.89 to 1 in light and 1.72 to 1 in dark, and the knob is the same colour as the card.
Reproduce: open /signup in dark and press Tab. See shots/x15-input-focus-dark.png, shots/x15-input-focus-light.png and shots/x17-switch-off-dark.png.
Great looks like: a focused field has a ring or border with at least 3 to 1 contrast against the field and the page, in both themes. It can stay neutral (for example the text colour) so red stays for errors. The off switch track or its outline reaches 3 to 1.

blockers.title: View only WMS and parts of Pulse still open full forms
blockers.where: apps/wms (dashboard 'Add client', /clients 'Create client' and 'Bulk import/update'); apps/pulse (/welcome 'Save the rate', /labor 'Add a labor class'); the ViewOnlyGuard marks in each app shell
blockers.detail:
Wrong: SPEC 9.4 says a person is told before a form opens. CRM and Projects now do this well. WMS and parts of Pulse do not.
- WMS, trial ended, red banner showing: 'Add client', 'Create client' and 'Bulk import/update' look fully live. 'Create client' opens the whole 4 step form. No control on the dashboard or /clients carries the `data-plan-write` mark.
- Pulse, paused: 'New job', 'Log work' and 'Add your first job' open the dialog (good). 'Other ways to start' goes to /welcome with a live 'Save the rate'. The setup 'Open' buttons go to /labor with a live 'Add a labor class'.
- The save is refused at the end with an inline error and a toast. The inline error wraps into three short lines beside the button.
- Pulse write buttons are not dimmed the way CRM dims Invite, Import and New board.
Reproduce: end a trial on an org with a WMS warehouse, open /clients and press 'Create client'. In a paused Pulse org press 'Other ways to start', then 'Save the rate'. See shots/x80-wms-vo-create-client--desktop-light.png, shots/x74-wms-viewonly--desktop-light.png and shots/x79-pulse-vo-save-rate--desktop-light.png.
Great looks like: every create and edit entry in the WMS and in Pulse settings, labor and welcome opens the same small view only dialog as CRM. Primary write buttons are dimmed in view only in all four apps. A browser test covers the WMS and these Pulse pages.

blockers.title: Locked Projects still opens the New task form, and it dead ends
blockers.where: apps/projects/src/features/shell/app-shell.tsx (top bar 'New task', the phone '+' button), apps/projects/src/features/quick-add/quick-add-dialog.tsx; lock frames in CRM, WMS, Projects and Pulse
blockers.detail:
Wrong: when Projects is not in the plan, the lock screen shows inside the full live app frame.
- The red 'New task' button in the header opens the complete New task dialog over the lock screen.
- You can type a task. 'Add task' then answers 'Pick a project for this task', and there are no projects. It never says the app is not in your plan.
- The four apps frame the lock two ways: CRM and WMS show a bare header (logo, org name, app switcher), while Projects and Pulse keep the whole nav and their create buttons.
Reproduce: in a trial without Projects, open Projects and press 'New task'. See shots/x03-projects-lock-newtask--desktop-light.png and shots/x71-projects-lock-addtask--desktop-light.png. Compare sheets/k-misc1.png (CRM lock) with sheets/k03-projects-lock-trial-A.png.
Great looks like: on a locked app the create buttons are hidden or disabled, or they lead to the lock card's own button. All four apps use one lock frame.

blockers.title: The first WMS screen in a trial is a bare form with 9 required fields
blockers.where: apps/wms/src/app/setup-warehouse/page.tsx and setup-form.tsx (reached from the launcher tile 'Open WMS' and the setup guide step 'Create your warehouse')
blockers.detail:
Wrong: a new customer who picks WMS and presses 'Open WMS' lands on 'Set up your warehouse'.
- Nine fields are all required: warehouse name, short code, contact name, street, city, state, postal code, contact phone and time zone. Nothing says so until you press the button and seven fields turn red at once.
- There is no line saying why we ask or that it can be changed later.
- 'Short code' is not explained.
- There is no way back to the Portal, no app header and no plan banner.
- The heading is small (text-lg) next to the 32 px headings elsewhere.
- On phones the inputs are about 30 px tall and the button 32 px.
- The signup promise in the spec is '4 fields, no phone, no wall'. This screen asks for a phone number on the second click.
Reproduce: start a trial with WMS and open http://localhost:3000. See sheets/k02-wms-trial-A.png, sheets/wms-phone.png and sheets/x72.png.
Great looks like: one friendly heading and one line of help. Only the name and time zone are needed to start; the address and contact are marked optional or asked later. 'Short code' has a plain hint. A 'Back to Portal' link is present. Fields are 44 px on phones. It uses the same page frame and type scale as the other first run screens.

blockers.title: Unknown portal addresses show the bare default 404
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/app (there is no root not-found.tsx); seen at /nope-not-here and /billing/nope, signed in and signed out
blockers.detail:
Wrong: any address the portal does not know shows the stock Next.js page: '404 | This page could not be found.' in tiny text on a plain white or black page.
- No logo, no header, no theme, no link back.
- /billing/nope gets it too. The billing section's own not found page only shows for a bad invoice id, where it looks good.
- SPEC rule 5 says no dead ends.
Reproduce: open http://localhost:3300/billing/nope. See shots/x41-billing-404--desktop-light.png and shots/a18-404--desktop-dark.png. Compare shots/x42-invoice-404--desktop-light.png, which is the good one.
Great looks like: a themed page in the portal frame with a plain sentence and two buttons, 'Back to my apps' and 'Go to Billing' (or 'Sign in' when signed out), in light and dark.

blockers.title: Organization page truncates names and emails on phones
blockers.where: apps/portal/src/app/(app)/settings/organization/page.tsx (members list, pending invitations); apps/portal/src/features/setup/setup-guide.tsx (header and step rows at 390 wide)
blockers.detail:
Wrong at 390 wide:

blockers.title: Small polish gaps a top product would not ship
blockers.where: Plan picker rows (yearly); portal launcher tiles and the shared view only message; apps/wms setup-warehouse 'needs plan' state; Pulse /jobs/new opened by address; invite form with the seat offer
blockers.detail:
Fix in one sweep:
1. Picker with yearly on: each app row shows '$29 per user each month' and right under it 'Your price: $236.64 per user each year'. Two units on two lines. Show both per month (for example '$19.72 per user each month, billed yearly') or both per year. See sheets/t5.png.
2. Mixed instructions when a plan exists but is late or paused. The banner says 'Pay now... Update card' or 'Start again now'. The launcher tile says 'View only. Pick a plan to make changes.' The refusal toast says 'Pick a plan in the Portal to make changes.' The WMS card is headed 'Pick a plan to set up your warehouse' with an 'Update card' button. Use the banner's words and button in all of them. See sheets/t13.png, sheets/k-misc2.png and shots/x79-pulse-vo-save-rate--desktop-light.png.

summary:
Verdict: not a pass. 6 blockers (3 backend, 3 ui). None is a fake charge, a double charge or an access leak. They are wrong or confusing words on money screens, a false line in the activity log, and console errors on the WMS first run.

**How I tested**
- I drove the real product with Playwright and direct calls against the shared dev stack, with the test gateway and the plan gate on.
- I made 7 new organizations and read `core.entitlements`, `billing_subscriptions`, `billing_invoices`, `billing_events`, `billing_emails` and the audit log after each step.
- I did not edit product code. Scripts and screenshots are in `/home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/opqa2/`.
- The Portal dev server was killed for lack of memory mid run. I restarted it once with `ENTITLEMENTS_DEV_ALLOW_ALL=0 deploy/dev/app-start.sh portal`. All six servers are up.

**Round 1 blockers I confirmed fixed**
- **Signup and picker:** a refresh keeps name, email, company and every picker choice. Duplicate email and wrong password no longer log console errors.
- **Promo code:** TEST10 shows when applied, and the success page, billing home and the invoice all say $355.68.
- **Credit:** billing home shows the balance and the real next charge.
- **Seats and invites:** open invites count toward the seat floor. Invited people arrive verified.
- **Billing managers:** the row is removed when the person leaves the organization.
- **Stale confirm:** it is caught with the "amount changed" message (the title is still wrong, see blocker 2).
- **Checkout sessions:** two sessions cannot both be paid. I raced two tabs twice and got one plan and one invoice each time.
- **WMS:** the owner dead end is gone, and the warehouse limit shows the price before the form and returns to the warehouses page.
- **Other:** the setup guide shows 5 steps, the email typo fix works, and the old flash no longer outlives its action.

**What works, with real results**
- **Wizard to signup:** back, forward and refresh hold. Bad inputs, a weak password and a duplicate email give the right message. A double click makes one account and one trial.
- **Trial:** rows are source trial, 14 days out. Adding and removing apps in the trial works from the lock screens.
- **Checkout:** declined, not enough money and 3DS fail write no rows. 3DS approve works.
- **Plan changes:** every preview I compared matched its invoice to the cent, for seats, warehouses, apps, the bundle and monthly to yearly and back.
- **Webhooks:** replays answer "duplicate". Six bad signature cases get 400 and no row. Forged deleted, paused, stale and cross org events changed no plan, access or email.
- **Failed payment:** past due on day 0, a retry email on day 3, the last day email on day 6, view only on day 7. A declined replacement card is refused, and a good card restored access in 1.6 seconds.
- **Cancel and pause:** cancel, keep, cancel again, ended, and paying again with no second trial all work. So do pause, undo, paused and start again.
- **Roles:** a member sees only the small card on 9 billing pages and gets 404 on the PDF and the export. An admin can read but replayed server actions answer "forbidden". A billing manager can manage.
- **Two orgs for one user:** switching works and invoices are isolated.
- **Phone and speed:** no sideways scroll at 390 px on 8 screens, zero server errors in six logs, and no billing page over 1.1 seconds.

**Things to know that are not blockers**
- App banners lag up to 60 seconds after a change that keeps full access, because of the per app cache. Good news shows at once. It is most visible right after a test tool skip.
- Credits count full days left and charges count the started day, so adding then removing a seat costs one day ($11.60 charged, $10.83 back). This is written down as intended; blocker 3 asks for the words to say so.
- Real Stripe, real email and Google or Microsoft sign in are still unrun, as the integrator said.

blockers.title: Out of order or repeated invoice events write false lines in the customer's billing activity
blockers.where: packages/billing/src/server/webhook.ts, cases 'invoice.payment_failed' and 'invoice.paid'; shown on /billing/activity and in /billing/activity/export
blockers.detail:
What is wrong: the handler fetches the invoice as it is now, then writes the activity row without checking that the invoice still matches the event. Access, plan state and emails stay correct; only the activity log is wrong.

Reproduce: run docs/billing/.review/opqa2/06-webhook.js against a paid org. It posts correctly signed events.
- An `invoice.payment_failed` for an invoice that is already paid added "We could not charge the Visa ending 3184 for $0.00."
- An `invoice.paid` for an already recorded invoice, under a new event id, added a second "Payment of $1,153.46 succeeded."
- It also added a credit line that contradicts the first one: "$1,329.95 credit is left" against "Your credit is used up."
- After two runs the org's activity and CSV held 3 copies of the payment and 2 false failures.

Why it matters: Stripe does not promise event order. A failed attempt event that arrives after the customer has paid is a normal case.

What great looks like:
- `payment.failed` is written only when the fetched invoice is still open with money due.
- Payment and credit rows are deduped per invoice (and per attempt), the way the receipt email already is with `receipt:<invoiceId>`.
- A test covers payment_failed after paid, and a second paid event.

blockers.title: After the "amount changed" reload, the confirm panel title still hides part of the change
blockers.where: /billing/plan confirm panel (change-preview), title built from the stale cart; packages/billing/src/server/changes.ts and the PlanPicker change mode
blockers.detail:
What is wrong: the stale check now works, but the reloaded panel keeps its old title. Confirming again does more than the title says.

Reproduce:
1. Tab 1: open /billing/plan?interval=yearly on a plan with 7 seats and press Review change. The panel reads "Switch to yearly".
2. Tab 2: add 1 seat and confirm. The plan is now 8 seats.
3. Tab 1: press Confirm change. It correctly refuses with "The amount changed while you were looking."
4. The reloaded panel is still titled "Switch to yearly". Its math lines read "Unused time on KitStak CRM (8 users)" and "KitStak CRM (7 users) for the next year".

A second Confirm would switch to yearly and also remove the seat a colleague just added. Nothing in the title or the main lines says so. Screenshot: docs/billing/.review/opqa2/shots/stale-reloaded.png

What great looks like:
- The title and summary are rebuilt from the fresh plan against the cart, for example "Switch to yearly and remove 1 seat".
- Or the cart is rebased on the new plan so the other person's change is kept, and the picker shows the new "Now" values before a second confirm.

blockers.title: Change preview states the wrong reason for the amount when account credit exists, and never explains the credit amount
blockers.where: Change preview copy for interval switches with a credit balance (packages/billing change preview words, shown in the /billing/plan confirm panel); credit preview line
blockers.detail:
1. Wrong sentence on a yearly switch with credit.
- Without credit the panel is right: "Due today. After $158.53 credit for the part you did not use. $1,514.27".
- With credit on the account it reads: "Due today. $1,338.83 for the 30 days left in this period, less $1,329.95 paid from your credit. $8.88".
- On another run it read "$1,411.33 for the 15 days left in this period, less $257.87 paid from your credit."
- $1,338.83 is a full year ($1,479.00) less the unused month. It is not a price for 30 days. The sentence is false, and an 8th grader cannot make it add up.
- Great looks like: "$1,479.00 for the next year, less $140.17 for the part of this month you did not use, less $1,329.95 from your credit."

2. Credit lines give no day count.
- Adding a seat reads "$11.60. For the 15 days left in this period."
- Removing it a moment later reads "You get $10.83 credit on your next bill." No reason is given for the lower number.
- Same for a warehouse: $139.60 charged, $130.29 back.
- The rule is written in packages/billing/src/proration.ts (a charge counts the started day, a credit counts full days only), but the customer is never told.
- Great looks like: the credit line says "for the 14 full days left", so the two numbers explain themselves.

blockers.title: A declined card on the invite seat offer looks like an email error and gives no way to fix the card
blockers.where: apps/portal /settings/organization invite form and seat offer (invite-seat-offer, invite-add-seat)
blockers.detail:
Reproduce:
1. Use a paid org with every seat taken and a card that fails on later charges.
2. Invite someone, then press "Add seat and send invite".

What happens: nothing is charged and no invite is sent, which is right. But the message "That card was declined. Try another card or call your bank." appears under the Email field. The Email input turns red as if the address were wrong. There is no "Update card" link anywhere on the page.

SPEC 6.3 says a decline comes with "Update card". The owner has to guess that the fix is in Billing. Screenshot: docs/billing/.review/opqa2/shots/seat-offer-declined.png

What great looks like:
- The decline shows inside the seat offer box, not on the email field.
- It has an "Update card" button to /billing?fix=payment that returns to the invite.
- The typed email is kept.

blockers.title: Console errors on the WMS first run path
blockers.where: apps/wms/src/app/setup-warehouse (POST /api/tenancy/warehouse) and apps/wms/src/app/(app)/layout.tsx redirect
blockers.detail:
The owner's rule is zero console errors. Two show up on the first WMS screen a trial customer sees.

1. Form validation is logged as an error.
- On http://localhost:3000/setup-warehouse, press "Create warehouse" with empty fields, or with a bad phone.
- The browser logs "Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 400 (Bad Request)" for POST /api/tenancy/warehouse.
- The inline messages are good. The console is not clean.
- Great looks like: required fields are checked in the browser before the call, or an expected validation answer comes back as 200 with an error body, as the portal forms now do.

2. The redirect logs two errors in the dev server.
- Opening the WMS root for an org with no warehouse, or with WMS not in the plan, redirects from /dashboard to /setup-warehouse or /locked.
- It logs: "Route "/dashboard": Could not validate `instant` because the target segment was prevented from rendering" and "An error occurred while attempting to validate instant UI", from AppLayout.
- Seen on every such open, in 3 separate runs.
- This one is dev mode only and the redirect predates this branch. But it is on the main trial path, and the owner will see it in a demo with dev tools open.
- Great looks like: the plan and warehouse redirect happens before the cached shell layout renders (a route level check or proxy), so the validation does not trip.

blockers.title: Test card "Fails at next renewal" does not fail at the next renewal when saved on the card page
blockers.where: packages/billing/src/gateway/test.ts attemptCharge (card.chargesSucceeded) and the test card page /test-gateway/card; docs/billing/DEV.md test cards
blockers.detail:
What is wrong: the test gateway lets a `fails_on_renewal` card succeed once after it is saved, whatever kind of charge comes first. So the chip's label is only true at first checkout.

Reproduce:
1. On an active plan, open Update card, tap "Fails at next renewal" (4000 0000 0000 0341) and save.
2. Skip ahead 30 days. The renewal is PAID with that card (invoice paid, plan active).
3. Only the renewal after that fails.

The opposite also happens. When 0341 is used at a pay today checkout, the next mid cycle charge (add a seat) is declined, though it is not a renewal.

This is the tool the owner uses to demo failed payments, and DEV.md says the card "works now and fails at the next renewal". No real money is involved.

What great looks like:
- A card saved through the card page starts with its one free charge already used, or the rule is tied to the charge reason (fail every `subscription_cycle` charge, allow the first charge and plan change charges).
- The chip label and DEV.md say exactly what happens.

blockers.title: Two checkouts opened at the same moment leave the plan cut off from every later gateway event: free access after cancel or a failed payment
blockers.where: /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing/src/server/checkout.ts (createCheckout: ensureCustomer, the core.stripe_customers upsert, expireOpenCheckoutSessions per customer; applyCheckoutSession), /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing/src/server/sync.ts (fetchAndApplySubscription ownership rule, refreshFromGateway), /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing/src/server/webhook.ts (fetchInvoice), /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing/src/jobs/reconcile.ts
blockers.detail:
createCheckout reads core.stripe_customers, then asks the gateway for a customer, then upserts. Nothing serializes this per organization. Two calls at the same moment (two tabs, or an owner and a billing manager) each make their own gateway customer, the last upsert wins, and both pay pages stay open because the 'only one pay page' guard expires sessions per customer. If the person pays the page of the customer that lost the upsert, applyCheckoutSession applies the plan (it checks the session, not the stored customer), but from then on fetchAndApplySubscription and fetchInvoice refuse everything for that plan with 'subscription does not belong to the org'.

Reproduced with the real code on the test gateway: `cd /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing && pnpm exec tsx ../../docs/billing/.review/sec2/probe-customer-race.mts` (hit on the second try). Real output: stored customer cus_test_8e6b..., plan row customer cus_test_1100...; ledger rows customer.subscription.created, invoice.paid, customer.subscription.updated and customer.subscription.deleted all 'ignored'; no receipt email and no payment.succeeded line for a $145.00 charge; the card update page opens for the wrong customer; refreshFromGateway answers no_subscription and the reconcile job cannot repair it. After a cancel and 40 days, the gateway subscription is 'canceled' while our row is still 'active', the entitlement row is 'active' and CRM access is 'full'. So a customer can pay one period, cancel (or let the card fail) and keep full access for good, and can do it on purpose because they control the timing. The same code runs for Stripe, where the customer create call makes the window wider.

Great looks like: (1) one customer per organization by construction: take lockOrgBilling (or insert the customer row first with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and read it back) before the gateway is asked; (2) close open pay pages by organization, not by customer; (3) when a checkout session of the organization is applied, the stored customer and the plan agree: either adopt the session's customer in the same transaction or cancel and refund a session whose customer is not the stored one; (4) the ownership rule also accepts the subscription id our own plan row holds; (5) reconcile logs loudly when a live plan cannot be refreshed; (6) a database test with two createCheckout calls in Promise.all that asserts one customer, one open session, and that a later renewal, cancel and failed payment event are 'processed'.

blockers.title: Billing actions land on whatever organization is active at the click, not the one the page shows: a stale tab changes another organization
blockers.where: /home/user/kitstak-platform/apps/portal/src/server/billing-actions.ts (contextFor and every action), /home/user/kitstak-platform/apps/portal/src/server/billing/context.ts (getBillingContext), /home/user/kitstak-platform/apps/portal/src/server/signup-actions.ts; the forms under /home/user/kitstak-platform/apps/portal/src/features/billing
blockers.detail:
No billing action carries the organization its page was rendered for. Each one reads the session's active organization at the moment of the click. A person in two organizations who switches organization in another tab and then presses a button in the first tab acts on the wrong organization, and the screen says it worked.

Reproduced in a real browser against the dev portal with `node /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/sec2/stale-tab.cjs` (probe account since removed): tab 1 opened /billing/details and showed 'Sec Probe Org A'; the active organization was switched to B the way the org switcher does it (organization.setActive); 'Save' in tab 1 answered as saved. Database after: Org A company_name empty, Org B company_name 'STALE TAB COMPANY A', and the activity line 'updated the billing details' is on Org B. The same holds by code for startCheckoutAction (a pay page for B with A's cart), cancelPlanAction, pausePlanAction, keepPlanAction, undoPauseAction, openCardUpdateAction, retryPaymentAction, startTrialAction (uses up B's one free trial), changeTrialProductsAction and the billing manager actions. Only confirmPlanChangeAction is safe, because the basis names the subscription. For Stripe the details write also overwrites B's customer name, address and tax ID.

Great looks like: every billing page passes the organization id it was rendered for to its actions; the server still uses the session's active organization, and refuses when the two differ with one plain sentence ('You switched organizations. Reload this page.'). This is a comparison, not trust in the browser, so SPEC 12.3 still holds. Add an action test for 'rendered for A, active is B: refused, nothing written' and one browser test with two tabs.

blockers.title: The same plan change confirmed at the same moment is applied and charged more than once
blockers.where: /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing/src/server/changes.ts (applyPlanChange: no lock between the basis check and gateway.applyChange), /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing/src/gateway/test.ts (applyChange reads and writes its documents with no lock)
blockers.detail:
applyPlanChange checks the basis, asks for a fresh preview, then calls the gateway, with nothing that makes these one step. Calls that arrive together all pass the basis check. Reproduced with `cd /home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing && pnpm exec tsx ../../docs/billing/.review/sec2/probe-race.mts`: preview for 1 to 5 CRM seats said $96.67 due; three confirms in Promise.all answered ok, ok, ok; the organization has three paid invoices of 9667 cents, four payment.succeeded lines, three plan.changed lines and four receipts for one change. Round 1 asked for a stale confirm to be caught; a stale basis sent later is now refused (verified: price_changed), but the same basis sent at once is not.

On real Stripe I expect the subscription update to be serialized so the money is taken once, but that is unverified (no keys), and the activity log would still say 'was charged for the days left' once per call with the amount from the preview, not from the invoice. The gateway everyone can run today charges three times.

Great looks like: the basis check and the apply run under the per organization lock (lockOrgBilling, or a claim row keyed on org and basis), so the second confirm sees the new basis and answers price_changed, or returns the finished state without a second call; the activity sentence takes its amount from the invoice the gateway returned; the test gateway makes applyChange atomic; a database test fires three confirms at once and asserts one invoice, one plan.changed row and one receipt.

summary:
Verdict: not a pass. Three backend blockers, each reproduced with real commands. The round 1 security fixes hold.

**What I ran**
- `pnpm exec vitest run` in `/home/user/kitstak-platform/packages/billing`: 24 files, 449 tests, all pass, with the database up.
- Four probe scripts and one browser script, all in `/home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/sec2/` (ignored by git).
- curl against the running dev portal, CRM, Projects and Pulse with a throwaway account, which I removed afterwards.

**Round 1 fixes that hold**
- **Proration:** eight upgrade and downgrade cycle patterns (seats, apps, bundle on and off, monthly and yearly flips, near a day boundary) never gave the customer a net gain. A stale basis and a wrong expected amount both answer `price_changed`.
- **Double checkout, one after the other:** the older pay page closes and one plan and one charge result. An unpaid session grants nothing. Another organization's session answers `not_found`.
- **Unverified inviter:** 403 `EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED` at the portal door and at the CRM's Better Auth door.
- **Microsoft sign in:** it is no longer a trusted link provider; only the `xms_edov` claim counts as a proven email (read in code, no keys to run it).
- **Webhooks:** no signature and a bad signature answer 400 and write no ledger row. The Stripe route answers 503 with no keys.
- **Cross organization reads:** another organization's invoice page, invoice PDF, test checkout page and test card page all answer 404. The activity export answers 404 when signed out.
- **Redirects:** ten `?next=` and `?return=` tricks all stayed on the portal origin.
- **Plan gate:** Projects outside the trial answers 402. CRM writes answer 402 `plan.read_only` once the trial is over, and reads still work.
- **Secrets:** none in the diff, and no `.env` file is tracked.
- **Production doors:** I read `billing-off.spec.ts` and the mode code but did not run a production build myself.

**Not blockers, but worth fixing**
1. **Real Stripe is still unrun.** The adapter reads sensibly, but pending updates, future proration dates and invoice previews have never met the real API.
2. **One trial per person is check then write.** Three trial starts at once by one person on three organizations all started (`trial-farm.mts`). It gives no extra days, only parallel trials.
3. **Billing email is a second mail door.** An unverified owner can set any billing email, and the trial reminder emails then go to that stranger. Volume is low, about four emails per trial.
4. **Reset codes allow about 100 guesses a day per address** (5 tries per code, 20 codes a day). Consider a lower day cap or a lock after several used up codes.
5. **Database tests skip silently** when Postgres is not reachable (`describe.skipIf`), and the repo has no CI file. A gate run without a database would be green with every money and webhook test skipped. Add a switch that makes them fail instead.
6. **A manual revoke is undone by a trial.** `setEntitlement` only protects a live manual grant, so starting a trial overwrites a row staff revoked by hand (read in code, not run).
7. **CRM invite routes send no email.** `/api/v1/invitations` and the wizard route write invite rows directly. No mail leaves, so it is not a spam door, but SPEC 5.5 says every invite sends an email, and the verified email rule does not run there.
8. **Database connections are held across gateway calls.** Sync runs gateway reads inside a transaction that holds the per organization lock. On the test gateway my probe starved a pool of 4 ("timeout exceeded when trying to connect"). On Stripe, a burst of events for one organization can hold all 5 portal connections for seconds.
9. **Query values can reach the ledger.** `errorText` of a failed query includes its parameters, and that text is stored in `core.billing_events.error`.

**One thing I changed in the shared dev database**
My first race probe called the reconcile job with a clock 40 days ahead. It stamped `gateway_synced_at` and `updated_at` on 20 other dev organizations with a 2027 date. I set both back to now for exactly those rows. Their status and entitlements were not changed.

Not passed. Head to head score is 22 of 30 with no zero (round 1 was 20 with one zero); the bar in COMPETITORS.md section 6 is 24 or more. Full scorecard: /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/reviews/critic-round-2.md. Scripts and screenshots: /home/user/kitstak-platform/docs/billing/.review/critic2/ (not committed).

How I tested: real Chromium against the shared dev stack with ENTITLEMENTS_DEV_ALLOW_ALL=0, three fresh signups. Riley (desktop, home page then /pricing cart) ran the whole flow: signup mistakes, change email, verify, welcome, all four apps, picker, review, pay page mistakes, promo, declines, bank approval, trial end, invoice and PDF, seat removal and credit, yearly preview, billing details and tax ID, pause, cancel, failed renewal and Pay now, invite at the seat limit, add Projects from inside Projects. Jo (360 px phone, dark, Pulse only) ran signup through launcher, then trial end and view only. Sam ran the wizard handoff by keyboard and the day 3 trial banner. I did not edit product code or restart servers; I ran deploy/dev/rate-limit-reset.sh once after the signup limit stopped me.

Round 1 blockers: 9 of 11 are fixed and verified in the browser (promo on every screen to the cent, credit named and applied, one "Pick a plan" name, short path from the home page, Change email, 5 step guide that stays 5, invoice and PDF that match the picker, trust and refund lines, the six small lines). The password blocker is half fixed (rules now shown, still four rules). Real Stripe is still unrun.

Why it is not a pass: billing is now excellent and beats the field on price math, invoices, failed payment, cancel and pause. The way in does not beat Linear, Slack or Stripe: a password with four rules, a WMS that opens on 8 required fields, a launcher that puts the buyer's own app last, three screens to reach a card field, and a signup panel that gives no reason to sign up. Two plan change sentences do not say what really happens (the yearly switch, and add versus remove on the same day). Finance still needs a paid seat. Real Stripe has never been run.

Not verified: Google and Microsoft sign in (no keys), real Stripe (no keys), the portal's Terms/Privacy/Talk to us links (they point at kitstak.com, unreachable here; I read the local site pages instead). Phone tap targets measured clean at 44 px with no sideways scroll.

blockers.title: Switching to yearly explains the amount with the wrong sentence
blockers.where: Portal /billing/plan confirm panel, monthly to yearly
blockers.detail: Saw: "Due today. $3,082.34 for the 23 days left in this period, less $51.04 paid from your credit. $3,031.30". An 8th grader reads that as $3,082 for 23 days. The amount is really one year at the new price less the unused part of this month; "See the math" shows that, and its unused time lines use 22 days, not 23. Reproduce: paid monthly plan, pick "Pay yearly", "Review change". Great: "Due today $3,031.30. One year at your new price is $3,321.12. You get $238.78 back for the unused part of this month, and $51.04 from your credit." Then "Then $3,321.12 per year, starting Nov 24, 2027." No "days left" wording on a change of billing period (SPEC 6.3 example reads this way).

blockers.title: A seat costs more to add than it gives back on the same day, and no screen says so
blockers.where: packages/billing/src/proration.ts (charge rounds days up, credit rounds days down); confirm panel words; site pricing rule 2; Terms section 4
blockers.detail: Saw on one day: "Add 1 seat" was "$17.79 for the 23 days left in this period"; "Remove 1 seat" was "You get $17.01 credit on your next bill" with no day count ($17.01 is 22 days). The site promises "You pay only for the days left" and "the unused part becomes credit". Slack's fair billing gives back what it takes. Great: either both directions use the same day count (stop the free credit trick another way, such as no credit for a seat added in the last 24 hours), or keep the rule and say it wherever it applies: panel reads "Credit for the 22 full days left", and the pricing page and Terms say "A day that has started counts as used." A buyer who checks the math must get our number.

blockers.title: The WMS opens on a wall of 8 required fields
blockers.where: WMS /setup-warehouse (first screen after "Open WMS" for a new trial owner)
blockers.detail: Saw: Warehouse name, Short code, Contact name, Street address, City, State, Postal code and Contact phone are all required. No trial line, no skip, no link back to the Portal, no app switcher. Signup promised 4 fields and no phone; "Start fresh" and "Explore sample data" both end here. Total typed fields to a first WMS screen: 12. Great: one required field (warehouse name, already filled as now), short code stays filled, address, contact and phone optional with "You can add these later in Settings", a "Back to Portal" link and the normal app frame. One click from "Open WMS" to a real WMS screen. Shopify asks for the address when you pick a plan.

blockers.title: The launcher puts the app you signed up for last
blockers.where: Portal launcher / (app tiles)
blockers.detail: Saw: Jo signed up for Pulse only. At 360 px the launcher shows the guide, then CRM, WMS and Projects tiles marked "Not in your plan" with prices, and only then Pulse with "Open Pulse", about three screens down. At 1280 by 800 the Pulse tile is below the fold too. Great: tiles in the plan or trial come first; the rest sit below under a small heading such as "More apps" with their price as now. On a phone the buyer's own app is on the first screen under the guide.

blockers.title: Three screens repeat the same math before a card field
blockers.where: Portal /billing/plan, then /billing/checkout, then the pay page (from the banner or billing home "Pick a plan")
blockers.detail: Saw: click 1 opens the picker with the saved cart and summary, click 2 the review screen with the same summary, click 3 the pay page with the same summary again plus the card form. Stripe Checkout is one click to a card field; Linear and Vercel put the card in settings. Great: two clicks at most. When the saved cart has not changed, "Pick a plan" goes straight to the review screen (it already has "Change my plan"), or the picker in pay mode gains the "First charge" fact and goes to the pay page. Keep the three facts, drop the repeat.

blockers.title: Signup still needs a password with four rules, and there is no other way in
blockers.where: Portal /signup, /reset-password, /invite; shared password policy in packages/auth
blockers.detail: Saw: "correct horse battery staple" (28 characters) is rated "Fair" and refused: "Your password still needs a capital letter and a number." The rules are now shown up front, but there are still four. Linear, Slack and Notion ask for no password; Stripe has no make up rules. Google and Microsoft buttons could not be seen (no keys). Great: any password of 15 characters or more passes with no other rule. Better: "Email me a code instead" using the existing 6 digit code flow, so the code is both sign in and verification. Plus one recorded run with Google and Microsoft test keys showing both buttons work on /signup and /login.

blockers.title: "Guests are free" has no door, roles have no price, and invites go one at a time
blockers.where: Portal /settings/organization "Invite someone" (setup guide step 2)
blockers.detail: Saw: pricing FAQ, picker and billing home say "Guests are free". The invite form offers Admin, Member and Viewer only; all three use a paid seat (usesSeat('viewer') is true) and the form does not say so. Two addresses with a comma give "Enter a valid email address." Great: a line under Role: "Admin, Member and Viewer each use 1 seat. Guest is free." with Guest in the list or a link to where guests are invited. The field takes several addresses. Before sending, one line says what it does to the plan ("Uses 1 of your 3 free seats", or the existing seat prompt).

blockers.title: Real Stripe has never been run end to end
blockers.where: packages/billing Stripe adapter, stripe:setup, /api/billing/webhooks/stripe, GO-LIVE.md Open item 1
blockers.detail: Unchanged from round 1: every payment in both reviews and the e2e suite used the test gateway. Hosted Checkout, wallets, Billing Portal card update, live webhooks, Stripe's invoice PDF and the future proration date are unseen. Great: one recorded run in Stripe test mode: stripe:setup check all ok; Checkout with the working, declined and bank approval cards; a promo code; a card update in the Billing Portal; a replayed webhook; for three carts Stripe's total equals our quote to the cent. Needs test keys from the owner.

blockers.title: The signup page gives no reason to sign up
blockers.where: Marketing home hero (apps/web) and Portal /signup right panel
blockers.detail: Saw: the form is clean, but the panel beside it is a drawing of four tiles and "One login. Every KitStak app your team runs on." Arriving from the home page it shows no price, no product and no proof. The hero "Start free" button has no "14 days free. No card needed." line near it. Great, nothing invented: that line under the hero button; on the signup panel three promises the product already keeps ("See your exact price before you start", "Cancel in two clicks. Pause for 1 to 3 months", "Nothing is deleted when a trial ends"), a real screenshot of each chosen app, the four list prices when there is no cart, and real customer proof when the owner has some.

blockers.title: The person who pays the bills must hold a paid seat
blockers.where: Portal /billing/team and /settings/organization
blockers.detail: Saw: "Add a billing manager" lists only current team members. With one person it says "Invite someone new in Organization", and that form has only paid roles. So giving the bookkeeper billing costs a seat ($23.20 a month here) and gives them the apps too, while the page urges "Add a second person so billing never gets stuck." Great: add a billing manager by email on the Billing team page; that person gets Billing only, uses no seat, and the page says "Billing only. Free. No access to your apps." Atlassian and Slack billing contacts work this way.

blockers.title: Small true things that add up
blockers.where: Portal /verify-email, /billing/checkout/success, billing help line, picker focus, invoice seller block; app shells after trial end
blockers.detail: (1) /verify-email breaks the address mid word ("carter-su" / "pply.example"). (2) Success page at 1280 by 800: two stacked bars push "Open my apps" under the fold. (3) For up to 60 seconds after a trial ends an app shows no banner and opens its create form (I opened "New job" in Pulse; the entitlement cache is 60 s). Clear the cache when the end date passes or check the date on each read. (4) "Talk to us" on billing pages opens a site form that only opens your email app, with no reply time. Great: the support address on the billing page and a reply time the owner can keep. (5) In local dev the Portal's Terms, Privacy and Talk to us links go to https://kitstak.com, not the local site as DEV.md says. (6) Arriving on the picker by keyboard, focus is on the body; 12 Tab presses to reach "Start my free trial". (7) Invoice seller block is "KitStak LLC, kitstak.com" with no address; owner must set BILLING_SELLER_* before launch.
